question: Does the statement form of a failure exit change /Oe region allocation although the instructions are the same? Positive control S25:39C7 DoDigInB (worker resI): the original keeps the GetEnterDirB result dir in DI up to the y == 0x3f test, then spills it to its home ([bp-4], 'mov [bp-4],di; mov cx,di') before nx/ny take DI/SI. That allocation appears only when the later DigTileThemB test is written 'if (DigTileThemB(nx, ny)) { ...dig... } else { BlistM[..] = GetNewModeB(caste); return; }' (the form of the red twin DoDigInR, root:0F3F); the negated early exit 'if (!DigTileThemB(nx, ny)) { ...; return; } ...dig...' compiles to the same instruction sequence except that dir stays in memory for the whole function (532 instead of 533 bytes). Region allocation of a split variable therefore depends on source structure far from the region itself (bisection: removing either the caste early return or the BlistT chain store also restores DI; one extra use of dir after newattr does too).
